subject: Whether the strings this product matches Logic's interface with are strings Logic ships
question: Of the literals AXLocalePolicy matches against, how many exist in Logic's own data, and what are the ones that do not?

reverify.expected: 379 distinct literals; 113 a QuickHelp Title, 226 elsewhere in the bundle, 40 nowhere
reverify.cost: ~40s; reads the app bundle, launches nothing

method: Extracted only the `canonical` and `variants` fields of every LabelSet -- a first pass that also swept `rationale` counted 185 unmatched, and most of those were documentation prose, not labels. Folded each literal the way this module folds canonical text (NFC, NBSP to space, strip) and compared case-insensitively, because every LabelSet match mode in the product folds case. Searched QuickHelp Titles across all ten locale names first, then every value in the bundle's .strings corpus.

the spelling Logic actually ships for the label this record lists as absent. `Set Locators…` is absent from all 23 corpora and that is true of the ELLIPSIS form only -- Apple ships the toolbar item without one, in ten locales, and the product carried the ellipsis. Recording the absence without this citation reads as `Logic has no such label`, which is the opposite of the finding. Apple does ship ellipses where a menu item opens a dialog (`Set Left Locator numerically…`), so their absence here is a fact about this string rather than a corpus that drops them

canon_absent.claim: the literals this product matches with that exist nowhere in Logic's shipped data
canon_absent.why_runtime: Each is either a label Logic composes at runtime, a label drawn from a framework outside this corpus, or a string that was typed rather than read. This record does not decide which; it establishes that no canonical source answers for them, which is the precondition for a measurement being the only route.

conclusion: Of the 379 distinct literals AXLocalePolicy matches Logic's interface with, 113 are a QuickHelp Title and 226 more are somewhere in the bundle's .strings corpus, leaving 40 that exist nowhere in Logic. Those 40 are not one kind. Roughly half are lowercase fragments used for containment matching and were never meant to be whole labels. The rest look like labels. Neither is a defect of the unfindable-element shape. `AXLocalePolicy` already carries Apple's spelling as the CANONICAL member of each set -- `Project or Section…` with U+2026 and `Autopunch` as one word -- and matching is variant-inclusive, so the element is found. What the canon axis shows is narrower and worth keeping: three of the tolerance VARIANTS beside those canonicals (`Project or Section...`, `프로젝트 또는 섹션...`, `Auto Punch`, `Auto-Punch`) are spellings Logic does not ship anywhere in this corpus. They cost nothing and may be deliberate tolerance for other builds -- the set's own comment says both renderings were observed -- but nothing in the tree could previously tell a tolerance variant from a typo, and now something can. Nothing here was changed: a string absent from the corpus is not thereby wrong, and this repository has already learned that editing a label by guess is what produced the German track-creation report.
limits: Case-folded comparison, because every LabelSet match mode in the product folds case. A guard stricter than the thing it audits refuses honest readings.

The .strings corpus is what Scripts/logic_canon.py extracts: 2,537 files. Strings compiled into nibs, into the binary, or into a framework outside the app bundle are not in it, so `nowhere` means `not in this corpus`, never `not in Logic`.
Presence does not mean the interface uses it. Measured separately: the live UI shows untranslated `German` and `MIDI Region` although ko translations for both keys exist.
Absence does not mean wrong. A label Logic composes at runtime is absent and correct; this record does not separate those from typed ones.
The two demonstrated defects were found by re-asking with a different character. Nothing systematically re-asked the other 38, so there may be more of the same shape.
A first pass that swept the `rationale` field as well reported 185 unmatched. That number is wrong and is recorded here only so it is not mistaken for a measurement if it surfaces elsewhere.

An earlier revision of this record called two of the forty 'demonstrably wrong' and said the product spells the Bounce leaf with three ASCII full stops. That was an overclaim, corrected after review: the product's CANONICAL spelling is Apple's in both cases and the three-dot forms are additional variants, so neither makes an element unfindable. The overclaim is the same class of error this axis exists to stop, which is why it is recorded here rather than quietly edited.

The nib limit this record named for itself was closed by #895 on 2026-09-16. Three of the ten strings it proved absent -- `Package`, `One File per Track`, `Delete Tracks and Content` -- are English Apple compiles into a Base.lproj nib, and they moved from the absence claim to citations. The counts in `observations` and `conclusion` are the 2026-09-15 reading over the corpus of that day and are not restated here; `reverify` prints today's.
